perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: 'by the end of the hour the child would have forgotten his clothes and would have acted as he would in old clothes' — the perfect is right for 'would have forgotten' (forgetting completed by that time point), but the acting-as-in-old-clothes behavior only BEGINS once the clothes are forgotten and continues onward; it cannot be an event completed by the end of the hour. The passage's own timeline contradicts the perfect: the child 'would be better behaved for a short period' (filling the earlier part of the hour). Required form: 'would act' or 'would be acting'. The 'Likewise' sentence confirms the intended sense of subsequent ongoing behavior ('might soon change ... and be no more noisy than usual'). Attempted rescue reading (normal acting finished within the hour) collapses the 'but by the end of the hour' contrast and clashes with the habitual 'as he would in old clothes'. Not defensible as written.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: 'while (he is) playing cowboys' — standard while + -ing ellipsis with matching subject 'the child'; 'play cowboys' is idiomatic for role-play games. Grammatical.
